title: Allow clean distinction of popover vs dialog.show() vs dialog.showModal() toggle events
body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

For web authors determining what exactly has happened upon receiving a `toggle` event is currently difficult or even impossible in some cases, yet the effects on the displayed UI and interactability can by drastically different, depending on the mechanism that caused the event.

### What problem are you trying to solve?

I need to book-keep open popovers, dialogs, selects' picker dropdowns, fullscreen elements (to track top-layer occupancy). A document root `toggle` event listener detects when a popover opens or closes; it also detects when a dialog opens or closes. (Events emitted for opening and closing select picker dropdowns is currently discussed [here](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11564); in the meantime my [polyfill](https://www.npmjs.com/package/select-events) providing custom `--select-open` / `--select-close` events is used; fullscreen elements can be detected via the `fullscreenchange` event.)
So I rely on `toggle` events for popovers and dialogs.
But accurately distinguishing the different cases is currently surprisingly hard and therefore error-prone, or even impossible (i.e. dialog toggle close modal vs regular [see](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/9733#issuecomment-2377675130)).

```html
<button popovertarget="my-dialog">Open dialog as popover</button>
<button onclick="document.getElementById('my-dialog').show()">Open as non-modal dialog</button>
<button onclick="document.getElementById('my-dialog').showModal()">Open as modal dialog</button>
<dialog id="my-dialog" popover></dialog>

<button popovertarget="my-details">Open details as popover</button>
<button onclick="document.getElementById('my-details').open = true">Open details as disclosure</button>
<details id="my-details" popover="manual"></details>
```

Each of the five buttons results in a `toggle` event with `newState: open` but only in three cases the top-layer changes. Looking at the event args alone is not sufficient. We have to perform additional checks on the target element like `element.matches(':popover-open')` or `element.matches(':modal')`.
When trying to distinguish a `toggle` event with `newState: closed` we can't even use the same check anymore, because the closed target element no longer matches `:popover-open` or `:modal`; which makes reliable book-keeping impossible without building additional data structures to keep element references.
Ideally a `toggle` event listener could determine from the event args alone which case it is - for opening as well as closing events.

### What solutions exist today?

Today we need to check `event.target.matches(':popover-open')` to determine whether a `toggle - newState: open` event is signalling an opened popover. We have no corresponding check to determine whether a `toggle - newState: closed` event is signalling a closed popover. We can only determine it indirectly by keeping a list of DOM element references that represents all currently open popovers.

We need to check `event.target.matches(':modal')` to determine whether a `toggle - newState: open` event is signalling an opened modal dialog caused by `dialog.showModal()`. We have no corresponding check to determine whether a `toggle - newState: closed` event is signalling a closed modal dialog. We can only determine it indirectly by keeping a list of DOM element references that represents all currently open modal dialogs.

We need to check `event.target.tagName === 'DIALOG' && !event.target.matches(':modal') && !event.target.matches(':popover-open')` to determine whether a `toggle - newState: open` event is signalling an opened non-modal dialog caused by `dialog.show()`. We have no corresponding check to determine whether a `toggle - newState: closed` event is signalling a closed non-modal dialog. We can only determine it indirectly by keeping a list of DOM element references that represents all currently open non-modal dialogs.

### How would you solve it?

I propose an additional property `cause` on [toggle event](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLElement/toggle_event) args that clearly conveys which web platform mechanism caused the toggle event, so web authors can use the property to reliably distinguish the different cases.

```ts
interface ToggleEvent {
    oldState: "open" | "closed"
    newState: "open" | "closed"
    cause: "popover" | "dialog.default" | "dialog.modal" | "details.default" | "select.default" | "select.popover"
}
```

This additional property would solve the current difficulties and provide a clear path for future element types and their respective toggle events:
- `toggle - newState: open - cause: popover` target was opened as a popover by the popover mechanism
- `toggle - newState: closed - cause: popover` target was closed as a popover by the popover mechanism
- `toggle - newState: open - cause: dialog.default` target was opened as non-modal dialog by `dialog.show()` or `dialog.open = true` (default toggle behavior)
- `toggle - newState: closed - cause: dialog.default` target was closed as non-modal dialog by `dialog.close()` or `dialog.open = false` (default toggle behavior)
- `toggle - newState: open - cause: dialog.modal` target was opened as modal dialog by `dialog.showModal()` (modal behavior)
- `toggle - newState: closed - cause: dialog.modal` target was closed as modal dialog by `dialog.close()` or `dialog.open = false` (modal behavior)
- `toggle - newState: open - cause: details.default` target was opened as disclosure element by `details.open = true` (default toggle behavior)
- `toggle - newState: closed - cause: details.default` target was closed as disclosure element by `details.open = false` (default toggle behavior)
- `toggle - newState: open - cause: select.default` target's picker dropdown opened by `select.showPicker()` or user interaction (default appearance behavior)
- `toggle - newState: closed - cause: select.default` target's picker dropdown closed by user interaction (default appearance behavior)
- `toggle - newState: open - cause: select.popover` target's picker dropdown opened in top-layer by `select.showPicker()` or user interaction (base-select appearance behavior)
- `toggle - newState: closed - cause: select.popover` target's picker dropdown closed in top-layer by user interaction (base-select appearance behavior)

### Related

- This issue is a spin-off from the discussion [toggle and beforetoggle events for the select element](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11564)
- Toggle events for dialog was discussed [here](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/9733)

More control over -or at least to query- the top-layer is a hot topic:
[API to get top layer elements](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/9075)
[Expose a stack of blocking elements](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/897)
[Expose an API to get the top layer element](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/8783)
[Feature Request: Top Layer Stack Management](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/10370)
